text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing intense itching and have developed red bumps on your thigh and other parts of your body. To better understand your condition, have you noticed if these bumps appear in clusters or have a central bite mark?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Prurigo Nodularis.

The patient is a 47-year-old male with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia presenting with intense itching and red bumps on the thigh, exacerbated after attending a conference in Miami. I am considering scabies or an insect bite reaction, but the chronicity of itching suggests a pruritic disorder. Given his travel history and medication list, could you confirm if the bumps are itchy at night or if anyone around you is experiencing similar symptoms?
